judged_text: Every request to /embed/best for an unknown embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no rate limit on the endpoint, and the per-URL 60s throttle inside the job is keyed on the full URL, so varying the path or query string bypasses it — each novel URL triggers a full HTTP fetch of the embeddable_host page and, on success, creation of a real topic. An anonymous client forging a Referer header can flood the sidekiq queue, pin workers on outbound fetches against the embedded site, and mint unbounded scraped topics in the forum's database, exhausting workers and storage on the request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `/embed/best` which, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` with no controller-side throttling (`EmbedController#best`). The only throttle is in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which keys Redis on the full URL string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying path/query produces a new key and bypasses the 60s limit. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` then calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` and can create a new topic/post/embed record for each novel URL on `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. `ensure_embeddable` relies on `request.referer` host equality, which is client-controllable, so an anonymous client can trigger unbounded job enqueues/outbound fetches/topic creation. This is a verifiable resource-exhaustion/spam vector introduced by the diff.
